title: An exception table check that rejects a handler range ending at code_length
summary: The class file reader checks each exception table entry as JVMS §4.7.3 requires: `start_pc` before `end_pc`, `end_pc` at most `code_length`, `handler_pc` inside the code. A developer makes the three offsets uniform, all of them less than `code_length`, reasoning that an offset into the code is an offset into the code. The property committed for the check is a throws clause, the specification's three conditions as the condition under which the reader throws `ClassFormatError`; the prover refutes the uniform check on the smallest method there is, one byte of code covered by a handler that ends where the code ends, which the patched reader rejects as malformed.

change.description: Check `end_pc` with the same comparison as `start_pc` and `handler_pc`: an offset inside the code, strictly less than `code_length`. The comment now says that all three are offsets into the code. The tests for well-formed entries, empty and inverted ranges, and ranges and handlers outside the code pass.

risk: `end_pc` is exclusive: the entry covers `[start_pc, end_pc)`, and a handler that covers the last instruction of a method has `end_pc == code_length`, an offset one past the code. javac emits such entries for every `try` whose body is the last thing in a method, which is most `try` blocks in most methods, so a reader that rejects them rejects most class files on disk with `ClassFormatError`. The specification explains the half-open range, and admits that it keeps a method of exactly 65535 bytes from protecting its last instruction, in the same paragraph. The tests check entries copied from `javap` output of a method with code after the `try`, in which no handler reaches the end of the code.
explanation: The property committed for `checkEntry` has no assertion, only a throws clause: `throws: ClassFormatError when startPc >= endPc || endPc > codeLength || handlerPc >= codeLength`, under the assumption that the four fields are `u2` and the code is not empty. JML calls this a `signals` clause; the tool reads it as two obligations, that the method throws `ClassFormatError` where the condition holds and returns where it does not, and compiles both into the generated harness, with a handler for the declared class (which JBMC has no model of, so the tool takes it and its superclass `LinkageError` from the JDK image) and a flag computed before the call. JBMC refutes the patched check at once, and the tool shrinks the witness: `checkEntry(startPc=0, endPc=1, handlerPc=0, codeLength=1)`, a method of one byte whose handler covers it, on which the patched reader throws `ClassFormatError` where the clause says no exception applies. The witness is the boundary the specification defines, and `end_pc` is the only field of the entry it affects.
resolution: Revert, and keep the comment that says why `end_pc` is compared differently: the range is half-open, so `end_pc` may equal `code_length`, as HotSpot's own check (`end_pc > code_length` is the error) has it. The throws clause is the regression test, and the shrunk witness is the unit test to add: a handler that covers the last instruction.
notes: The throws clause of the property brings the exceptional path under the proof.
Rejects every handler that covers the last instruction of a method, since `end_pc == code_length` is allowed.

Gap scan (step 1a of `llm-dlc/loops/sound-verdicts.md`, 5 November 2026, JDK 25.0.4.1, from the bytecode, nothing proved): the tool's own checker meets no gap in the 1 method the proof reaches, so strict mode does not move this verdict. The recorded proof is JBMC's, which strict mode of the tool's own checker does not change. JBMC's own approximations are step 4c's.
provenance: Constructed from the exception table checks of JVMS §4.7.3, by making the three offset checks uniform.
